architecture.mechanism: Thermoelectric generators convert heat into electricity across a temperature difference, which is sustained by using a high-power radiative cooling film as the cool end.
architecture.intervention: Mount TEG modules on the engine's exhaust manifold/block (hot side) with the radiative cooling film applied to the cold side, wiring the recovered electricity into the vehicle's alternator/battery system.
architecture.expected_effect: Engine waste heat is converted into electrical power, cutting thermal energy loss and raising overall engine efficiency with no extra emissions and only thin-film packaging.
architecture.falsification_test: Road-test an engine with a film-equipped TEG versus a bare TEG at identical exhaust temperatures; if power density and temperature gradient do not exceed the bare-module baseline, the mechanism is falsified.
